page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no marginal notes. Running head at the top, page number at the top right, catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: tio. Inde quasi dubitans, ecquod tandē adhiberi utiliter posset remedium: Per quid, inquit, percutiemini vltrà? Scitè uidelicet depingit affectus pij patris, qui dum de filij salute, quem cernitne plagis quidem emendari, prope desperat, secum etiamnū deliberat, an cedere uelit amplius. Omnia sunt pathetica, et singula membra ingens habent pondus. Quinetiam tacitè rursus exaggeratur hic Iudæorum peccatum, ab eo quòd iam antea toties experti grauissima mala, tamen in uiam nondum redierint.

Omne caput languori.) Per congeriem, & similitudine sumpta à corpore humano, quod undique morbis scatet, ægritudinibusq; est infectum, uaria commemorat pericula, quæ omnium ordinum homines in Iudæa perpessi fuerant. Diuersa membra corporis, diuersos ordines in ciuili societate pulchrè repræsen-tant. Nisi quis malit hic describi simpliciter, primò ægritudines & contagiosos corporum morbos, deinde bella & strages, euersiones ciuitatum, necnon affinia mala diuinitus immissa. Porrò non tantùm loquitur de malis quæ pertulerant Iudæi temporibus Vsiæ, quæ tamen neque parua, neq; pauca fuisse certum est, præsertim ubi huic regi totics aspera bella fuerunt gerenda cum hostibus, ubi item immensi sumptus impendi ad apparatum militarem, ad extruendas munitiones & machinas bellicas: uerùm de illis quoq;, quæ uisa fuerunt sæpe antea apud illorum maiores, quæ pro-

page.notes: The paragraph opening "Omne caput languori.)" is a commentary lemma in the running text, not a heading. Short dashes at several line ends are printer's rules, not text, and are left out. Underlined words in the text are not marks. The catchword is hard to read and is given as "scita" with [?]. The line-end word "uelit" is split across lines without a printed hyphen, so it is written whole. Possible printing errors: "tantùm" and "uiam" are as printed.
